payload.set_intro: Researchers tested a cognitive therapy for social anxiety. They randomly assigned 100 adults with social anxiety to receive eight weekly sessions of the therapy or to a waiting list that received the therapy after the study. In the therapy sessions, clients learned to identify and challenge negative thoughts such as 'everyone will think I am boring.' Anxiety was measured with a questionnaire (higher scores mean more anxiety) before and after eight weeks. Participants in the study gave informed consent. The mean decrease in anxiety score was 18 points in the therapy group and 4 points in the waiting-list group. The researchers reported that the effect size was 0.9 and the difference was statistically significant (p < .01).

stimulus.description: The study description above is the only material shown with these questions.

items.stem: The therapy sessions taught clients to identify and challenge negative thoughts. This technique is most closely associated with which type of therapy?

options.why: Person-centered therapy uses active listening and unconditional positive regard.
Psychodynamic therapy uses free association and dream interpretation.
Aversion therapy applies conditioning to link a behavior with an unpleasant outcome.
Cognitive therapy uses techniques such as cognitive restructuring to change maladaptive thinking.

items.explanation_en:
The correct answer is Cognitive therapy. Cognitive therapy uses techniques such as cognitive restructuring to change maladaptive thinking.
Person-centered therapy is incorrect: Person-centered therapy uses active listening and unconditional positive regard.
Psychodynamic therapy is incorrect: Psychodynamic therapy uses free association and dream interpretation.
Aversion therapy is incorrect: Aversion therapy applies conditioning to link a behavior with an unpleasant outcome.
